title: Hibari Misora's birth chart
metaDescription: Hibari Misora's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 7.3° Gemini. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The chart's headline is a trine: Mercury and Neptune within 0.0°, thinking wired to imagination. A third of the circle is the tradition’s friendliest distance — same element, shared assumptions, no translation required.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 7.3° Gemini — the first decan, 0°–10°, which the tradition sub-rules by Mercury. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Gemini and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 16.2° Taurus, Venus was at 26.0° Aries, Mars was at 25.1° Scorpio. Read together: a mind that trusts the measured and the checked; taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate; drive that moves on certainty and current.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest — Mercury trine Neptune, 0.0° of separation. Trines are read as inheritance rather than achievement: the ease is genuine, and nothing about it was earned. Behind it, Jupiter opposition Pluto at 0.0°, and Venus square Pluto at 1.0° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: Jupiter opposes Pluto while both square Venus. Two squares braced against one opposition make a t-square — the chart’s working end, where pressure keeps finding the same outlet. The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, five sit in a sign it has an opinion about. The Moon in Capricorn at 19.1° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Venus in Aries at 26.0° is in detriment; Mars in Scorpio at 25.1° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Jupiter in Capricorn at 27.0° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Saturn in Aries at 3.2° is in fall. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Among the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the elements divide 5 earth, 2 fire, 2 water, 1 air; by modality, 5 cardinal, 3 fixed, 2 mutable. Earth weights a chart toward the material and the durable — what can be built, kept, and relied on. Mars and Jupiter were retrograde — the backward drift a body appears to make as the Earth overtakes it, read in the scheme as a function that reviews before it releases.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Capricorn for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.2° between midnight and midnight. Whatever the unrecorded hour was, it happened inside one Moon sign — the degree floats, the sign holds. At the noon reference it stands at 19.1°.
